title: Troubleshooting Managed Identity with Azure SQL
description: Diagnose the common failures when an Azure-hosted app uses a managed identity to connect to Azure SQL, and fix them with contained users, correct token scopes, and least-privilege grants.

data.text: Azure SQL supports SQL authentication (username and password) and Entra ID authentication. Entra ID authentication includes managed identities, which remove the need to store SQL credentials anywhere.
When using a managed identity, Azure SQL validates the token issued by Entra ID. You create a contained database user mapped to the external identity.

data.title: Azure SQL Auth Methods
items: SQL Authentication — username/password stored in SQL
Entra ID Universal with MFA — interactive user login
Managed Identity — passwordless for Azure-hosted apps

data.title: Create a Contained User for a Managed Identity
data.content: Map a managed identity to a database user so it can connect to Azure SQL.

data.title: Connection String with Managed Identity (C#)
data.content: Use SqlClient with Azure.Identity for passwordless SQL authentication.

data.text: Common failures and how to diagnose them

This lesson focuses on what goes wrong after you have enabled the identity. Module 6 covers the happy path in detail; here the goal is to recognize the handful of errors that account for almost every managed identity failure against Azure SQL.

rows: No contained database user for the identity
Create the user with CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER in the target database
CREATE USER ran in master, or the identity is not in the tenant
Connect to the application database, not master, and use the exact identity name
Cannot find the user because it does not exist
Caller lacks directory read permission, or the Entra admin is missing
Set an Entra ID admin on the logical server and grant Directory Readers if needed
Token requested for the wrong resource
Developer credential used locally; identity not attached or authorized
Attach the identity and verify the role or database user in Azure

data.title: Inspect database principals and role membership
data.content: Run this in the application database as an Entra administrator. External users have type E (Entra user) or X (external user or group).
data.code:
SELECT name, type, type_desc, authentication_type_desc
FROM sys.database_principals
WHERE type IN ('E', 'X');

SELECT dp.name AS member_name, r.name AS role_name
FROM sys.database_role_members rm
JOIN sys.database_principals r ON rm.role_principal_id = r.principal_id
JOIN sys.database_principals dp ON rm.member_principal_id = dp.principal_id
WHERE dp.name = 'shop-api';

data.text: CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER asks Azure SQL to look up the identity in Microsoft Graph. That lookup needs an Entra ID administrator on the logical server and, for service principals and groups, directory read permission. A clean pattern is to sign in as the server Entra admin, run the statement in the user database, and grant only the roles the app needs. If the identity is a group, create the user for the group and add the managed identity to that group in Entra ID.

data.title: Create a contained user and grant least privilege
data.content: Prefer explicit table permissions or a custom role over db_owner. The identity name must match the managed identity or group name exactly.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: A reliable answer to "the managed identity cannot connect to SQL" is a checklist: identity attached, token scope correct, contained user created in the right database, Entra admin configured, and firewall or private endpoint reachable. Naming the 18456 error and the scope https://database.windows.net/.default shows hands-on experience.

data.title: Connect an App to Azure SQL
data.description: Enable managed identity on an App Service, create an Azure SQL database user, and query data without a SQL password.
steps: Create an Azure SQL database and set an Azure AD admin.
Enable managed identity on your App Service.
Run T-SQL to create a contained user FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER.
Update your app to use DefaultAzureCredential with SqlClient.
data.expectedOutcome: Your app connects to Azure SQL using a managed identity with no password stored anywhere.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Managed identity removes the need for SQL authentication passwords.
CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER maps an Entra ID identity to SQL.
DefaultAzureCredential + SqlClient provides a clean passwordless pattern.
